assessment.title: Interpreting measurement evidence
assessment.diagnostic_focus: Distinguish score consistency, measurement uncertainty, and evidence supporting a particular score interpretation.

design.section_summary: Interpret measurement statistics without treating them as definitive proof of validity or exact individual scores.

objectives.statement: Evaluate what measurement evidence does and does not support in context.
evidence_requirements: Explain why internal consistency alone does not establish validity.
Identify the need for evidence when a test is used for a new purpose.

misconception_hypotheses.statement: High reliability is sufficient to establish validity for any use.
student_language_examples: A reliable test must be valid.
misconception_hypotheses.why_plausible: Students may conflate consistency with the meaning or appropriateness of a score interpretation.

generation_settings.context_notes: Treat distractor choices as hypotheses requiring reasoning evidence, not diagnoses. Keep the reading load low: short stems, plain wording and only the context each question needs.

items.stem: A class quiz shows high internal consistency (alpha = .90) in this year's class. What does this result alone tell the teacher?

options.label: A
options.text: The quiz scores support every planned use.

options.label: B
options.text: The items gave consistent results in this class.

options.label: C
options.text: Each student's score has no measurement error.

options.label: D
options.text: The quiz will be just as consistent in any class.

items.target_reasoning_note: Distinguish score consistency from the validity of a score interpretation.
essential_elements: Internal consistency describes how consistently the items worked together in this class.
Consistency alone does not establish what the scores mean or whether a use is justified.

distractor_rationales.A: Treats high reliability as evidence that the scores support any use.
distractor_rationales.C: Treats a reliable quiz as giving exact individual scores, overlooking measurement error.
distractor_rationales.D: Treats reliability as a fixed property of the quiz rather than of scores from a particular group.

items.stem: Maya scores 72 on a test with a standard error of measurement (SEM) of 4. What does the 4 describe?

options.label: A
options.text: How well the items measure the intended skill

options.label: B
options.text: How far Maya's score is from the class mean

options.label: C
options.text: How much error Maya's score of 72 may contain

options.label: D
options.text: How suitable the test is for other groups

items.target_reasoning_note: Recognize that an observed score carries measurement error, which the SEM describes.
essential_elements: The SEM describes how much an observed score may differ from the true score.
Maya's true score is likely near 72, but it is not known exactly.

distractor_rationales.A: Confuses score precision with evidence about what the items measure.
distractor_rationales.B: Confuses the standard error of measurement with the spread of scores across students.
distractor_rationales.D: Treats a precision statistic as evidence that the test suits other groups.

items.stem: A test built for course placement is proposed for licensing nurses. What should happen first?

options.label: A
options.text: Collect evidence for the licensing use

options.label: B
options.text: Use it if its reliability is high

options.label: C
options.text: Use it because placement worked well

options.label: D
options.text: Reject it because of its original purpose

items.target_reasoning_note: Evaluate whether there is evidence for a proposed new use of test scores.
essential_elements: A new use needs evidence for that interpretation, population and use.
Existing evidence neither transfers automatically nor rules the new use out.

distractor_rationales.B: Treats high reliability as enough evidence for a new use.
distractor_rationales.C: Assumes validity evidence for one use carries over to another.
distractor_rationales.D: Rejects a new use outright instead of weighing the evidence for it.
